chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated that from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Regarding a man and a boy who jointly participated in killing a man and so killed him, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: If the boy has reached five spans, qisas is carried out against him; and if he has not reached five spans, judgment is made with the diyah.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the authority giving this legal ruling
key_terms.اشْتَرَكَا: They jointly participated or shared in the act
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: Blood money or legal compensation for homicide
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَشْبَارٍ: A bodily measure used here as the legal threshold mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.غُلَامٍ: A boy or young male involved in the killing
key_terms.قَتْلِ: The act of killing or homicide

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man and a boy jointly kill someone in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning a man and a boy who jointly commit homicide. It states that if the boy has reached the measure of five spans, qisas applies to him; otherwise, the ruling is by diyah.
